Title: Illegal argument exception when extracting .tgz file 
Type: Bug | Priority: Major | Status: Resolved | Resolution: Not A Problem

Description:
When attempting to unpack a .tgz file, I am receiving the illegal argument exception: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Invalid byte 0 at offset 5 in '05412{NUL}11' len=8. This is causing a java.io.IOException: Error detected parsing the header error. 

This is being thrown when the function TarArchiveInputStream.getNextTarEntry() is called. 

Here is the code I am using. 

{code:java}
            TarArchiveInputStream tarIn = new TarArchiveInputStream(
                    new GZIPInputStream(
                            new BufferedInputStream(
                                    new FileInputStream(
                                            tempDirPath + fileName))));

            TarArchiveEntry entry = tarIn.getNextTarEntry();

            while (entry != null) {
                File path = new File(tempDirPath, entry.getName());
                if (entry.isDirectory()) {
                    path.mkdirs();
                } else {          
                    path.createNewFile();
                    byte[] read = new byte[2048];
                    BufferedOutputStream bout = new BufferedOutputStream(new FileOutputStream(path));
                    int len;
                    while ((len = tarIn.read(read)) != -1) {
                        bout.write(read, 0, len);
                        System.out.print(new String(read, "UTF-8"));
                    }
                    bout.close();
                    read = null;
                }
                entry = tarIn.getNextTarEntry();
            }
            tarIn.close();
{code}

[Collin Molnar]: Example .tgz file with error.

[Collin Molnar]: Also this .tar file is made using a python script, with the tarfile library.

[Stefan Bodewig]: Thanks, Collin.  Can we distribute the file as a unit test resource?

According to  the spec the number fields should be padded with NULs, looks as if the library just inserted a single NUL.  Our current implementations strips NULs starting at the right, which fails here.  It should be easy to fix by breaking out of the loop as soon as a NUL is detected.

[Sebb]: I don't see the Exception when running the code using current trunk.

I tried both the code in the description (though I omitted writing any files) and the Lister class.
Both ran successfully.

@Colin: Maybe you could try using the 1.10-SNAPSHOT build from the ASF snapshot repo:
https://repository.apache.org/content/repositories/snapshots/

Does this fail for your sample program?

[Collin Molnar]: Thank you Stefan and Sebb. It seems that my issue is when I'm downloading the file using the commons.net.FTPClient, and it seems somehow when I download the file it is being corrupted. 

Frustratingly enough, the corrupted file is still a valid tar file so I assumed the issue with was compress. So I will have to see if I need to change the encoding of the client, or if I need to do something else.
